NJD has been the better team at creating chances, taking 60% of the expected goals at five on five against 52% for NYR, and it generates 3.74 expected goals per 60 to NYR's 3.39. The Rangers allow slightly fewer (2.78 per 60 against 2.89), though the results haven't matched the process on either side: NYR has allowed 1.75 goals a game while NJD has given up 3.67. On special teams, the Devils' penalty kill gives up 0.63 expected goals a game to NYR's 0.41, while NYR's power play (0.74) has been a touch sharper than NJD's (0.65). New York takes 4.25 penalties a game, which could feed a Devils power play, and the model sees a close game, with 3.08 expected goals for NYR and 2.98 for NJD.

In net, projected starter Dylan Garand (NYR) is at .951 and +3.29 goals saved above expected this season, with +3.88 over three games last year. NJD's projected starter Jake Allen is at .885 and -1.32 this season, though he was +5.39 over 37 games last season, so a rebound is plausible.

Both teams have 1 day of rest. NYR is 4-1-0 in its last five with 56% of the expected goals, while NJD is 2-3-0 with 54%, including a 5-4 overtime win at DET on Tuesday. The model likes Jack Hughes most for NJD, with a 34% chance to score and 29% for two or more points. For NYR, Alexis Lafrenière is at 34% to score, and Mika Zibanejad is at 30% to score and 27% for two or more points.
